userRequest:
You are an agent version tracker. Check for new releases of the ORIGINAL upstream agent CLI products — NOT our babysitter plugin packages.

STEP 1: Build atlas.
```
npm run build --workspace=@a5c-ai/atlas
```

STEP 2: Get the target list using the SAME logic as `scripts/sync-external-plugin-repos.mjs` uses in `buildTargetsFromCatalog()`. Read that file to understand the pattern, then run the provided catalog descriptor command. This gives every agent that has an external repo. `externalPackageName` is the npm package to check if set. For agents without an npm package, search the web. Also check adapter source for additional install commands with `grep -r 'npm install -g' packages/adapters/codecs/src/ | grep -v node_modules | grep -v test`. Merge both lists. EXCLUDE all @a5c-ai/* packages.

STEP 3: For EACH upstream agent, check the latest published version. Use `npm view <package>@latest version` for npm packages. Search the web for agents distributed differently.

STEP 4: Compare against AgentVersion records in `packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/agent-versions/` and `packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/products/`.

STEP 5: For new versions not in the graph, search release notes/changelog/blog posts, create or update AgentVersion YAML, and note capability changes, new CLI flags, breaking changes, transport/API changes.

STEP 6: If graph files changed, rebuild `npm run build --workspace=@a5c-ai/atlas`, branch `agent-versions/daily-2026-07-12`, commit all changes, and create one PR against staging.

STEP 7: For each new agent+version pair, check for an existing issue with `gh issue list --label "agent-version-update" --search "<agent> <version>"`. If none exists, create an issue with labels `agent-version-update,graph-update`. The issue body must include exact old/new versions, actual release links, real change summaries, likely affected system surfaces, install/package status, migration notes, and a specific assimilation checklist tied to the changes.

STEP 8: Print a summary table with ALL agents checked.

IMPORTANT: Cover every upstream agent systematically. Do not stop after one. One PR for all changes in this run.
